JOIN Ben
CALL
JOIN Cat
CALL
JOIN Dan
END
check.expect:
Nobody waiting
Calling Amy
Calling Ben
Left: 2

pr.t: Walk a linked list in arrays
pr.tz: 遍历 array 表示的 linked list
pr.task: A linked list is stored in lists D (content) and NP (next index, −1 = null). Write walk(D, NP, start) returning the contents in list order, and length(NP, start) returning the number of nodes.
pr.taskz: Linked list 存在 D（内容）和 NP（下一个 index，−1 = null）。写 walk(D, NP, start) 按链的次序返回内容 list，和 length(NP, start) 返回 node 数。
pr.solution:
def walk(D, NP, start):
    out = []
    cur = start
    while cur != -1:
        out.append(D[cur])
        cur = NP[cur]
    return out

def length(NP, start):
    n = 0
    cur = start
    while cur != -1:
        n += 1
        cur = NP[cur]
    return n

pr.task: Lists D, NP (−1 = null) and the start index are given. Write insert(D, NP, start, n, name, i) which stores name at free index i so it becomes the n-th node, and returns the (possibly new) start. Write delete(NP, start, n) which removes the n-th node and returns the new start. Set the new node's pointer before changing the previous node's pointer.
pr.taskz: 写 insert(D, NP, start, n, name, i)：把 name 放在空位 i，成为第 n 个 node，返回 start；写 delete(NP, start, n)：删第 n 个 node，返回新 start。先改新 node 的 pointer。

tests.call: (lambda D, NP: show(D, NP, insert(D, NP, 0, 4, 'Brian', 4)))(['Iris','Ada','Peter','Ben',''], [1,2,3,-1,-1])
(lambda D, NP: show(D, NP, insert(D, NP, 0, 1, 'Zed', 4)))(['Iris','Ada','Peter','Ben',''], [1,2,3,-1,-1])

cards.en: Searching means finding the record(s) in a list or array whose value is the same as a target value. It is one of the most common tasks of a program: checking whether a student ID exists, looking up a price, finding the position of a name. The design of a search algorithm depends on whether the list is sorted. For an unsorted list the only safe method is linear search, because the target could be anywhere. For a sorted list we can use binary search, which is much faster for long lists. A search usually produces either a Boolean result (found / not found) or the index of the item, with a special value such as -1 meaning 'not found'. When you answer exam questions, always state: the list type (sorted / unsorted), what is returned, and how many comparisons are needed.
cards.zh: Searching（检索）就是在 list/array 中找出与 target value 相同的记录，例如检查学号是否存在、查价钱、找名字的位置。算法设计取决于 list 是否 sorted：unsorted list 只能用 linear search，因为目标可能在任何位置；sorted list 可以用 binary search，项数多时快很多。搜索结果通常是 Boolean（找到/找不到）或者 index，并用特殊值如 -1 代表“找不到”。答题时要讲清楚：list 是否已排序、返回什么、需要多少次比较 (comparisons)。

ex.q: A program stores 2000 unsorted product codes. A user types a code. Which search method must be used and what should the program return if the code is missing?
ex.a: The list is unsorted, so linear search must be used (binary search needs a sorted list). If the code is not found, return a value that cannot be a valid index, e.g. -1, or set a Boolean flag found = False.
ex.az: list 未排序 → 只能 linear search；找不到就返回 -1 或 found = False。

cards.tz: 线性搜索 Linear search（for 循环）
cards.en:
Linear search (sequential search) compares the target with the item at index 0, then index 1, 2, ... until the target is found or the last index is reached. It is simple and does not require the list to be sorted. The simplest Python version uses a for loop and a Boolean variable found:
found = False
for i in range(0, len(mark)):
    if target == mark[i]:
        found = True
print(found)
Key point: a for loop always runs len(mark) times, so it makes N comparisons whether or not the target is found, even if the target is the very first item. This is correct but wasteful. The improved version (next card) uses a while loop to stop early.
cards.zh: Linear search（线性/顺序检索）：由 index 0 开始逐个与 target 比较，index 1、2……直到 找到 target 或到达最后一个 index。优点是简单，不要求 list 已排序。最简单的 Python 写法用 for 循环加 Boolean 变量 found（见左/上方程序）。重点：for 循环一定执行 len(mark) 次，所以 不论找没找到都比较 N 次，即使目标在第一项也一样。结果正确但浪费，改良版用 while 循环提前结束。

ex.q: mark = [62, 50, 71, 88, 50]. Using the for-loop version with target 62, how many comparisons are made, and what is printed?
ex.a: The for loop visits i = 0,1,2,3,4: 5 comparisons. mark[0] = 62 so found becomes True. Output: True. Even though it was found at the first item, the loop continues.
ex.az: for 循环一定比较 5 次；第一项已找到，输出 True。

cards.t: Linear search with a while loop and a flag
cards.tz: Linear search：while 循环与旗标 Flag
cards.en:
A flag is a variable that records the state of a program, for example found. Because it has only two states it is a Boolean variable: set it to False first (assume not found) and change it to True when the target is found ('raise the flag'). Adding found == False to a while condition makes the loop stop as soon as the target is found:
found = False
i = 0
while i < len(mark) and found == False:
    if target == mark[i]:
        found = True
    i = i + 1
print(found)
Note i has already moved one past the found item when the loop ends, so the position is i - 1. Best case: 1 comparison; worst case (last item or absent): N comparisons.
cards.zh: Flag（旗标）是记录程序状态的变量，例如 found。只有两种状态，所以用 Boolean：先设 False（假设找不到），找到时改为 True（“举起旗子”）。在 while 条件加入 found == False，一找到就离开循环，提高效率。注意：离开循环时 i 已经多加了 1，所以位置是 i - 1。Best case 比较 1 次；worst case（在最后或不存在）比较 N 次。

ex.q: mark has 10 items and the target is at index 2. Compare the number of comparisons of the for version and the while+flag version.
ex.a: For version: always 10. While version: compares index 0, 1, 2 then found = True and the loop stops: 3 comparisons. After the loop i = 3, so the index is i - 1 = 2.
ex.az: for 版 10 次；while 版 3 次就停，位置 = i - 1 = 2。

cards.tz: 输出所有位置的 linear search
cards.zh: 如果 unsorted list 可能有 重复值，而要输出 所有相同值的 index，就 不能在第一次找到时停下，要用 for 循环走完整个 list。用 index = -1 记录有没有找到（-1 不是合法 index，代表“找不到”）。同一方法也可以统计出现次数（count = count + 1）或返回位置 list。这种情况比较次数一定是 N，因为每一项都要检查。

ex.q: mark = [70, 50, 64, 50, 91]. Target 50. What is output? What if target is 99?
ex.a:
Matches at index 1 and 3, so the output is 
1
3
For 99 nothing matches, index stays -1, output: No result is found.
ex.az: 50 → 输出 1 和 3；99 → index 仍为 -1，输出 No result is found.

cards.en:
Efficiency of a search is measured by the number of comparisons. For a list of N items using the early-stopping linear search:
  • Best case: target is the first item, 1 comparison.
  • Worst case: target is the last item or not in the list, N comparisons.
  • Average case: (1 + 2 + ... + N) / N = (N + 1) / 2, roughly N/2.
So the time grows linearly with N: double the list, double the work. That is fine for short lists but slow for long ones. A common exam trap: sorting the list does not make the ordinary linear search faster on average, the algorithm still checks items one by one.
cards.zh:
搜索效率用 比较次数衡量。N 项 list 用可提前结束的 linear search：
  • Best case：target 是第一项，1 次
  • Worst case：在最后一项或不存在，N 次
  • Average：(1+2+…+N)/N = (N+1)/2 ≈ N/2
时间随 N 线性增长：list 长一倍，工作量多一倍。短 list 没问题，长 list 就慢。常见陷阱：把 list 排序后，普通 linear search 的平均次数 不会减少，因为它仍是逐项比较。

ex.q: A class list has 500 names. Find best, worst and average comparisons for linear search.

cards.t: Linear search in pseudocode (comparison in the loop condition)
cards.tz: Pseudocode：在 while 条件中比较
cards.en:
DSE pseudocode often puts the comparison directly in the while condition and uses arrays starting at index 1:
i <- 1
while i <= n AND participant[i] != name do
    i <- i + 1
if i <= n then
    registered <- True
else
    registered <- False
The loop moves on while the current item is not the target. It stops either because the name is found (then i <= n and i is the position) or because i becomes n + 1 (not found). So after the loop the test i <= n tells whether the target exists. Order matters: i <= n is tested first so that participant[n+1] (out of range) is never accessed. Number of comparisons with names: 1 if it is the 1st name, k if it is the k-th, n if absent.
cards.zh: DSE pseudocode 常把比较直接写在 while 条件里，array 由 index 1 开始。当前项 不是 target 就继续；循环停下有两种原因：找到（此时 i <= n，i 就是位置），或 i 变成 n+1（找不到）。所以离开循环后用 i <= n 判断是否找到。条件次序很重要：先检查 i <= n，避免读取 participant[n+1] 越界。第 k 个名字要比较 k 次，不存在要比较 n 次。

ex.q: participant = [Amy, Ben, Cat, Dan] (n = 4), name = 'Cat'. Trace i and state registered.
ex.a: i = 1: Amy != Cat, i = 2; Ben != Cat, i = 3; participant[3] = Cat, condition false, loop ends. i = 3 <= 4, so registered = True, 3 comparisons.
ex.az: i 由 1 → 3，第 3 项相同时停；3 <= 4，registered = True，比较 3 次。

cards.t: Linear search on a sorted list
cards.tz: 已排序 list 上的 linear search
cards.en:
Misconception: 'Once the list is sorted, linear search becomes faster.' Correct: the ordinary algorithm does not change; on average it still needs about N/2 comparisons. To take advantage of the order we must change the condition. In an ascending list, once we reach an item larger than the target, every later item is also larger, so the target cannot be there. Add and target >= mark[i]:
i = 0
while i < len(mark) and target > mark[i]:
    i = i + 1
found = i < len(mark) and mark[i] == target
For a descending list use target <= mark[i] instead. This mainly improves the 'not found' case, which no longer always costs N comparisons.
cards.zh: 误解：list 排好序后 linear search 就会变快。正确：算法本身不变，平均仍约 N/2 次。要利用排序，必须改 条件：升序 list 中一旦遇到 比 target 大的项，后面全都更大，target 不可能在后面，所以加 and target >= mark[i] 提前停止。降序 list 则用 target <= mark[i]。这主要改善“找不到”的情况，不再一定要比较 N 次。

ex.q: Ascending list [12, 25, 31, 47, 58, 66, 80] and target 30. How many items are examined with the improved search?
ex.a: 12 < 30 continue, 25 < 30 continue, 31 > 30 stop. 3 items examined, 31 != 30 so not found. Ordinary linear search would examine all 7.
ex.az: 看到 31 > 30 就停，只检查 3 项；普通 linear search 要 7 项。

cards.tz: 二分搜索 Binary search 概念
cards.en:
Binary search works only on a sorted list. For an ascending list:
  1. Compare the target with the middle item. If equal, stop.
  2. If the middle item is smaller than the target, the target can only be in the second half; if larger, only in the first half.
  3. Repeat on the remaining half until the item is found or the range is empty (not found).
Each comparison removes half of the remaining items, which is why it is so fast. It is like looking up a word in a dictionary: open in the middle and decide which half to keep. Key phrase to memorise: 'The list must be sorted; the search range is halved after each comparison.'
cards.zh:
Binary search（对分/二分检索）只适用于 sorted list。以升序为例：
  1. 先比较 中间项 (middle item)，相同就结束；
  2. 中间项 小于 target → 只可能在 后半部分；大于 → 只可能在 前半部分；
  3. 在剩下一半重复，直到找到或范围变空（找不到）。
每次比较都 删去一半项目，所以很快，就像查字典：从中间翻开，再决定留哪一半。要背的句子：The list must be sorted; the search range is halved after each comparison.

ex.q: Explain in words how binary search finds 'M' in the sorted letters A to Y (25 letters).
ex.a: Middle item is the 13th letter M: found in 1 comparison. If the target were 'T' (20th): middle M < T, keep 14th to 25th; middle of that is the 19th S < T, keep 20th to 25th; middle 22nd V > T, keep 20th to 21st; middle 20th T found: 4 comparisons.
ex.az: M 正好是中间项，1 次找到；找 T 则 M→S→V→T 共 4 次。

cards.t: Binary search: start, mid and end
cards.tz: Binary search 的 start / mid / end
cards.en:
A program keeps two indexes, start and end, for the first and last positions of the current search range, and calculates mid = (start + end) // 2 (integer division, rounding down). After comparing mark[mid] with the target (ascending list):
  • equal: found at mid;
  • target < mark[mid]: end = mid - 1;
  • target > mark[mid]: start = mid + 1.
Note it is mid - 1 and mid + 1, not mid, because mid has already been checked. When start > end the range is empty and the target is not in the list. In exam trace tables, write start, end, mid and the item compared on each row.
cards.zh: 程序用 start、end 记录当前搜索范围首尾的 index，并计算 mid = (start + end) // 2（整数除法，向下取整）。比较 mark[mid] 与 target（升序）：相同 → 在 mid 找到；target 较小 → end = mid - 1；target 较大 → start = mid + 1。注意是 mid ± 1，因为 mid 已检查过。当 start > end 时范围为空，即找不到。做 trace table 时每行写 start、end、mid 及比较的项。

ex.q: mark = [50,51,64,65,75,79,80,85,88,97] (index 0-9). Trace a binary search for 80.
ex.a:
startendmidmark[mid]action
0947575<80, start=5
5978585>80, end=6
5657979<80, start=6
66680found
Found at index 6 after 4 comparisons.
ex.az: mid 依次为 4、7、5、6，比较 4 次，在 index 6 找到。

cards.zh: 课本的升序 binary search 程序见上。要记住：开始时 start = 0, end = len - 1；循环条件 start <= end，范围变空就停；flag found 令找到后马上离开循环。int((start + end)/2) 对非负数与 // 结果相同。写成 function 时通常 return mid，找不到 return -1。

ex.q: Write a function bsearch(a, t) that returns the index of t in ascending list a, or -1.
ex.a:
def bsearch(a, t):
    start, end = 0, len(a) - 1
    while start <= end:
        mid = (start + end) // 2
        if a[mid] == t:
            return mid
        elif t < a[mid]:
            end = mid - 1
        else:
            start = mid + 1
    return -1
bsearch([3,8,15,21,40], 21) returns 3; bsearch([3,8,15,21,40], 9) returns -1.
ex.az: return 代替 flag：找到即 return mid，循环结束仍未找到 return -1。

cards.t: Binary search on a descending list
cards.tz: 降序 list 的 binary search
cards.en:
If the list is in descending order the directions are reversed. If the middle item is greater than the target, the target must be in the second half (start <- mid + 1); if smaller, in the first half (end <- mid - 1).
Sub-program SearchByBinary(target)
  start <- 1
  end <- N
  while start <= end do
    mid <- (start + end) // 2
    if age[mid] = target then return mid
    else if age[mid] > target then start <- mid + 1
    else end <- mid - 1
  return -1
Exam tip: before writing binary search code, check the sort order given in the question and whether the array starts at index 0 or 1. Getting the direction wrong makes the search look in the wrong half and miss items.
cards.zh: list 是 降序 (descending) 时方向相反：中间项 大于 target → target 在 后半（start <- mid + 1）；中间项较小 → 在前半（end <- mid - 1）。答题提示：写 binary search 前先看清题目的排序方向，以及 array 由 index 0 还是 1 开始。方向写错会在错的一半找，导致找不到。

ex.q: age = [60, 52, 47, 33, 21, 15, 9] (index 1-7, descending). Search for 15.
ex.a: start=1,end=7,mid=4: age[4]=33 > 15 → start=5. mid=(5+7)//2=6: age[6]=15 → return 6. 2 comparisons.
ex.az: mid=4 的 33 > 15，去后半；mid=6 找到，返回 6。

cards.en:
In a sorted list equal values are next to each other. To count how many times a value occurs: first use binary search to find any position index of it, then expand left and right while neighbours have the same value.
Sub-program rightMost(index)
  right <- index
  while right < N AND age[right+1] = age[index] do
    right <- right + 1
  return right

Sub-program leftMost(index)
  left <- index
  while left > 1 AND age[left-1] = age[index] do
    left <- left - 1
  return left
Number of occurrences = right - left + 1. If the binary search returns -1, the count is 0. The bound checks (right < N, left > 1) come first so we never read outside the array.
cards.zh: sorted list 中相同的值 相邻。要统计某值出现次数：先用 binary search 找到它的 任一位置 index，再向左右扩展，邻居相同就继续。出现次数 = right - left + 1；binary search 返回 -1 则次数为 0。边界检查（right < N、left > 1）要放在前面，避免读取 array 以外。

ex.q: age (index 1-8) = [30,25,25,25,25,18,18,12]. Binary search for 25 returns index 4. Find the count.
ex.a: rightMost: age[5]=25 → right=5; age[6]=18 stop → right = 5. leftMost: age[3]=25 → 3, age[2]=25 → 2, age[1]=30 stop → left = 2. Count = 5 - 2 + 1 = 4.
ex.az: right=5，left=2，次数 = 5-2+1 = 4。

cards.t: Efficiency of binary search: log2 N
cards.en:
Each comparison halves the range: N, N/2, N/4, ..., N/2i. In the worst case we continue until one item is left: N/2i = 1, so 2i = N and i = log2N = log N / log 2. The maximum number of comparisons is this value rounded up (for a not-found search it can be ⌊log2N⌋ + 1, which is the same as rounding up unless N is a power of 2).
  • Best case: target is the first middle item, 1 comparison.
  • Worst case: about ⌈log2N⌉ comparisons.
Calculators' log key is base 10, so use log N ÷ log 2. Growth is very slow: 1000 items need about 10 comparisons, 1 000 000 items only about 20.
cards.zh: 每次比较后范围减半：N → N/2 → N/4 → … → N/2i。worst case 一直分到剩 1 项：N/2i = 1，即 i = log₂N = log N / log 2。最多比较次数取 向上取整。Best case：第一次的中间项就是 target，1 次；Worst case：约 ⌈log₂N⌉ 次。计算机的 log 键是 base 10，要用 log N ÷ log 2。增长非常慢：1000 项约 10 次，一百万项约 20 次。

ex.q: Find the maximum number of comparisons of binary search for N = 10 and N = 300.

cards.tz: Linear search 与 Binary search 比较
cards.en:
Linear searchBinary search
Design / codingSimpleMore complicated
List requirementNone (sorted or unsorted)Must be sorted
Max comparisonsN⌈log2N⌉
Average(N+1)/2about log2N
Suitable forSmall listsLarge lists
The larger N is, the bigger the advantage of binary search. However, keeping a list sorted has a cost: a new item must be inserted at the correct position (shifting other items), whereas linear search can just append it at the end. So choose by asking: does the program search more often or add items more often?
cards.zh: 见比较表。N 越大，binary search 优势越明显。但保持 list 有序有代价：新项要插入正确位置（其他项要移动），而 linear search 的 list 可以直接 加在末尾 (append)。所以要先问：程序 较常搜索还是 较常加入新项？经常搜索、很少新增 → binary search；经常新增、很少搜索或 list 很短 → linear search。

ex.q: A library system has 80 000 books, adds about 10 books a day and handles thousands of searches a day. Which search is better? Justify.
ex.a: Binary search. Searches are far more frequent than additions; worst case is ⌈log280000⌉ = 17 comparisons vs 80 000 for linear search. The extra cost of inserting 10 books a day in order is small.
ex.az: 搜索远多于新增，binary search 最多 17 次比较对比 linear 80000 次，插入成本小。

cards.en:
Swapping (exchanging the values of two variables) is the basic operation behind most sorting algorithms. Like swapping the drinks in two cups, you need a third cup, a temporary variable:
temp <- A
A <- B
B <- temp
Misconception: writing A <- B then B <- A does not swap. After the first line the original value of A is lost, so both variables end up holding the original B. A swap always needs 3 assignments, and this cost is used when comparing how efficient sorting algorithms are (fewer data movements is better).
cards.zh: Swapping（交换）即交换两个变量的值，是大部分排序算法的基本操作。就像交换两杯饮料要用 第三个杯，需要临时变量 temp。误解：直接写 A <- B 再 B <- A 并不能交换，第一句后 A 原本的值已丢失，两者都变成原来的 B。一次 swap 需要 3 次赋值，比较排序效率时也会考虑这个成本（数据搬动越少越好）。

ex.q: A = 7, B = 3. Show the values after each line of (i) the temp swap and (ii) the wrong version A <- B; B <- A.
ex.a: (i) temp=7; A=3; B=7 → swapped. (ii) A=3; B=3 → both 3, the 7 is lost.
ex.az: (i) 正确交换得 A=3,B=7；(ii) 两个都变 3，7 丢失。

cards.tz: 交换 array 两项的 sub-program
cards.en:
Sorting programs swap items inside an array, so we write a reusable sub-program:
Sub-program Swap(A, m, n)
  temp <- A[m]
  A[m] <- A[n]
  A[n] <- temp
It exchanges A[m] and A[n]. When data are kept in parallel arrays (e.g. athlete[i] and result[i] describe the same person), a sort on one array must swap the same pair of positions in every parallel array, otherwise names and results no longer match. In Python the sub-program can be:
def swap(a, m, n):
    temp = a[m]
    a[m] = a[n]
    a[n] = temp
Lists are passed by reference, so the change is seen by the caller.
cards.zh: 排序时要交换 array 内的两项，所以写成可重用的 sub-program Swap(A, m, n)，交换 A[m] 与 A[n]。若数据存于 平行数组 (parallel arrays)（如 athlete[i] 与 result[i] 是同一个人），对其中一个排序时，所有平行数组都要交换同一对位置，否则名字和成绩就对不上。Python 的 list 以 reference 传入 function，所以 function 内的修改调用者也看得到。

ex.q: athlete = ['Kit','Ann','Leo'], result = [12.8, 11.9, 12.1]. After sorting by result ascending using swaps on result only, what goes wrong?
ex.a: result becomes [11.9, 12.1, 12.8] but athlete stays ['Kit','Ann','Leo'], so Kit appears to have 11.9 s. Correct: swap the same positions in both arrays, giving athlete = ['Ann','Leo','Kit'].
ex.az: 只交换 result，名字就配错；两个 array 都要交换同一位置。

cards.t: Swapping in Python and without temp
cards.tz: Python 一行交换与不用 temp 的交换
cards.en:
Enrichment. Python supports tuple assignment, so a swap can be written in one line without a temporary variable:
x, y = y, x
mark[i], mark[j] = mark[j], mark[i]
The right-hand side is evaluated first, then assigned. For numbers there is also an arithmetic trick using a sum:
d <- A[a] + A[b]
A[a] <- d - A[a]   # becomes the old A[b]
A[b] <- d - A[a]   # becomes the old A[a]
This works only for numbers (and can overflow in some languages), so in exams the temp method is the standard answer unless the question asks for another way.
cards.zh: 延伸内容。Python 支持 tuple assignment，一行就能交换，不需临时变量：x, y = y, x。右边先计算，再一起赋值。数字也可用加减交换（先求和 d，再 d 减去另一个）。这方法只适用于数字（某些语言可能溢出），所以考试中除非题目要求，标准答案仍是 temp 方法。

ex.q: A = [5, 9]. Apply d <- A[0] + A[1]; A[0] <- d - A[0]; A[1] <- d - A[0]. Show each step.

cards.en: Sorting means arranging data in ascending (smallest first, A to Z) or descending (largest first) order. Everyday examples: sorting a spreadsheet by marks, File Explorer listing files by name or date modified, a price-comparison website listing products from cheapest. Sorting matters for two reasons: sorted data are easier for people to read (top scorers, cheapest items), and a sorted list allows a faster search (binary search). Most basic sorting algorithms split the list into a sorted part and an unsorted part; each pass moves one more item into the sorted part. Strings are compared by character codes, so 'Apple' < 'Banana', and capital letters come before small letters.
cards.zh: Sorting（排序）就是把数据按 ascending（由小到大、A 到 Z）或 descending（由大到小）排列。例子：spreadsheet 按分数排序、File Explorer 按名称或修改日期排列、比价网站按价钱排列。排序有两个作用：方便人阅读（最高分、最便宜），以及令 list 可以用 较快的 binary search。大部分基本排序算法把 list 分成 sorted part 和 unsorted part，每一 pass（轮）令 sorted part 多一项。字符串按字符编码比较，所以 'Apple' < 'Banana'，大写字母排在小写之前。

ex.q: Put ['pear','Fig','apple','Kiwi'] in ascending order as Python compares strings.
ex.a: Capital letters (code 65-90) come before small letters (97-122): ['Fig', 'Kiwi', 'apple', 'pear'].
ex.az: 大写字母编码较小，结果 ['Fig','Kiwi','apple','pear']。

cards.tz: 选择排序 Selection sort：概念与步骤
cards.en:
Selection sort is based on linear search. In each pass it searches the unsorted part for the largest (or smallest) item and swaps it with the first item of the unsorted part. The sorted part grows by one item per pass, at the front of the list.
Example, mark = [45,70,66,82,55,95,60] in descending order:
  • Pass 1: max 95, swap with 45 → [95,70,66,82,55,45,60]
  • Pass 2: max of rest 82, swap with 70 → [95,82,66,70,55,45,60]
  • Pass 3: 70 swaps with 66 → [95,82,70,66,55,45,60]
  • Pass 4: 66 already in place → no change
  • Pass 5: 60 swaps with 55 → [95,82,70,66,60,45,55]
  • Pass 6: 55 swaps with 45 → [95,82,70,66,60,55,45]
At most one swap per pass, so selection sort moves data few times.
cards.zh: Selection sort（选择排序法）以 linear search 为基础：每一轮在 unsorted part 找最大（或最小）值，再 与 unsorted part 的第一项交换。sorted part 在 list 前端，每轮多一项。左边例子是 [45,70,66,82,55,95,60] 降序排列的每一轮结果：95 与 45 交换、82 与 70 交换……若最大值已在正确位置（第 4 轮）就没有变化。每轮 最多交换一次，所以数据搬动次数少。

ex.q: Show T = [62, 48, 75, 30, 55] after each pass of selection sort in ascending order.
ex.az: 每轮找最小值放到 unsorted part 最前：30、48、55、62。

cards.en:
Descending selection sort from the textbook:
for i in range(0, len(mark)):
    max_index = i
    for j in range(i+1, len(mark)):
        if mark[j] > mark[max_index]:
            max_index = j
    temp = mark[i]
    mark[i] = mark[max_index]
    mark[max_index] = temp
i is the first position of the unsorted part; the inner loop is a linear search for the index of the maximum, starting from i + 1 because mark[i] is the initial guess. For ascending order use min_index and mark[j] < mark[min_index]. The outer loop can stop at len - 2 (range(0, len(mark)-1)): when only one item is left in the unsorted part it is already in place. Pseudocode version: for i from 0 to N-2 ... Call swap(i, min_index).
cards.zh: 课本的降序 selection sort 见上。i 是 unsorted part 的第一个位置；内循环是 linear search，找最大值的 index，由 i + 1 开始，因为 mark[i] 本身是初始假设。改为 升序：用 min_index，条件改 mark[j] < mark[min_index]。外循环做到 len - 2 就够（range(0, len(mark)-1)），因为最后只剩一项时它已在正确位置。pseudocode 写法：for i from 0 to N-2 … Call swap(i, min_index)。

ex.q: Write an ascending selection sort function that sorts a list of names alphabetically.
ex.a:
def selection_sort(a):
    for i in range(len(a) - 1):
        m = i
        for j in range(i + 1, len(a)):
            if a[j] < a[m]:
                m = j
        a[i], a[m] = a[m], a[i]
    return a
selection_sort(['Leo','Amy','Kit']) → ['Amy','Kit','Leo'].
ex.az: 用 min index，内循环从 i+1 开始，最后交换。

cards.en:
Count comparisons. In pass i (i = 0, 1, ...) the unsorted part has N - i items, and finding the maximum needs N - i - 1 comparisons. Total:
(N - 1) + (N - 2) + ... + 2 + 1 = N(N - 1)/2.
This number is the same for every input: selection sort always does the full searches, even if the list is already sorted, so its best, average and worst cases have the same number of comparisons. Number of swaps is at most N - 1. For 7 items: 7 × 6 / 2 = 21 comparisons. Starting the inner loop at j = i instead of i + 1 adds a useless comparison of an item with itself each pass; running the outer loop one extra time (to N - 1) gives the same result with no benefit.
cards.zh: 计算比较次数：第 i 轮 unsorted part 有 N - i 项，找最大值要 N - i - 1 次比较。总数 = (N-1)+(N-2)+…+1 = N(N-1)/2。这个数 对任何输入都一样：即使 list 已排好，selection sort 仍要完整搜索，所以 best/average/worst 的比较次数相同。交换最多 N - 1 次。7 项 → 7×6/2 = 21 次。内循环若由 j = i 开始，每轮会多一次自己跟自己比较；外循环多做一轮也不会改变结果，只是浪费。

ex.q: How many comparisons does selection sort make on 20 items that are already sorted?
ex.a: Selection sort does not detect sorted input: 20 × 19 / 2 = 190 comparisons.

cards.tz: 插入排序 Insertion sort：概念与步骤
cards.en:
Insertion sort divides the list into a sorted part (initially just the first item) and an unsorted part. Each pass takes the first item of the unsorted part as the key value, compares it with items in the sorted part from right to left, moves (shifts) the items that are in the wrong order one place backwards, then inserts the key into the gap. It is like arranging playing cards in your hand.
Example [45,70,66,82,55,95,60], descending:
  • key 70: 45 shifts → [70,45,66,...]
  • key 66: 45 shifts, stop at 70 → [70,66,45,82,...]
  • key 82: 45, 66, 70 shift → [82,70,66,45,55,95,60]
  • key 55: 45 shifts → [82,70,66,55,45,95,60]
  • key 95: all shift → [95,82,70,66,55,45,60]
  • key 60: 45, 55 shift → [95,82,70,66,60,55,45]
cards.zh: Insertion sort（插入排序法）把 list 分成 sorted part（开始时只有第一项）和 unsorted part。每轮取 unsorted part 第一项作 key value，由右至左与 sorted part 比较，把次序不对的项 向后移一位 (shift)，最后把 key 插入空位。就像整理手上的扑克牌。左边是 [45,70,66,82,55,95,60] 降序的每轮结果：key 70、66、82、55、95、60 依次插入正确位置。

ex.q: Show T = [62, 48, 75, 30, 55] after each pass of insertion sort (ascending).
ex.az: 每轮把 key 插入左边 sorted part 的正确位置。

cards.en:
Descending insertion sort:
for i in range(1, len(mark)):
    key = mark[i]
    j = i - 1
    while j >= 0 and key > mark[j]:
        mark[j+1] = mark[j]
        j = j - 1
    mark[j+1] = key
The outer loop starts at 1 because the first item alone is already a sorted part. j scans the sorted part from right to left; j >= 0 must be tested first to avoid reading mark[-1] (in Python that would silently read the last item!). Each shift copies an item one place back; after the loop, j + 1 is the gap where the key goes. For ascending order change the condition to key < mark[j].
cards.zh: 降序 insertion sort 见上。外循环由 1 开始，因为第一项自己已是 sorted part。j 由右至左扫描 sorted part；要先检查 j >= 0，避免读取 mark[-1]（Python 中会悄悄读到最后一项！）。每次 shift 把一项复制到后一位；循环结束后 j + 1 就是 key 的位置。改为 升序：条件改为 key < mark[j]。

ex.q: Trace the pass i = 3 for ascending insertion sort on [48,62,75,30,55].
ex.az: key 30，75、62、48 依次后移，j=-1 停，放到 index 0。

cards.en:
In one pass the key at position K (counting from 1) needs:
  • best case: 1 comparison, 0 shifts (already in place);
  • worst case: K - 1 comparisons and shifts (it goes to the front).
For the whole list (sorting into descending order): best case is when the list is already in descending order, about N - 1 comparisons and no shifts; worst case is when it is in ascending order (the reverse), needing 1 + 2 + ... + (N - 1) = N(N - 1)/2 comparisons and shifts. So insertion sort is very fast for lists that are almost sorted, e.g. adding a few new records to a sorted list, unlike selection sort which always makes N(N-1)/2 comparisons.
cards.zh: 一轮中位于第 K 位（由 1 数）的 key：best case 比较 1 次、不用移动（已在正确位置）；worst case 比较及移动 K - 1 次（要插到最前）。整个 list（排成降序）：best case 是 list 本来已是降序，约 N - 1 次比较、无移动；worst case 是 list 本来是升序（完全相反），需 1+2+…+(N-1) = N(N-1)/2 次。所以 insertion sort 对 接近有序的 list 非常快，例如在已排序 list 加入少量新记录；selection sort 则永远要 N(N-1)/2 次比较。

ex.q: Ascending insertion sort on [10,20,30,40,50] and on [50,40,30,20,10]: how many shifts each?
ex.a: Already ascending: 0 shifts (4 comparisons). Reverse order: 1+2+3+4 = 10 shifts = 5×4/2.
ex.az: 已排序 0 次移动；完全相反 10 次 = N(N-1)/2。

cards.t: Insertion sort: swap version vs shift version
cards.en:
Insertion sort can be written in two ways. Swap version: swap the key with its left neighbour repeatedly until it is in place. Every swap costs 3 assignments, so moving the key back 3 places costs 9 assignments.
Shift version: copy the key into a variable, shift the 3 larger items one place right (price[j+1] <- price[j], 3 assignments), then put the key in the gap (1 assignment): about 5 assignments including saving the key.
Conclusion: the shift version is more efficient because it moves data fewer times, even though the number of comparisons is the same. Exam answers should mention 'fewer data movements / assignments'.
cards.zh: Insertion sort 有两种写法。Swap 版：把 key 与左边邻居一直交换直到正确位置；每次 swap 要 3 次赋值，向后移 3 位就要 9 次。移位版 (shift)：先把 key 存进变量，把 3 个较大的项各向右移一位（3 次赋值），最后把 key 放入空位（1 次），连保存 key 共约 5 次。结论：移位版较有效率，因为数据搬动次数较少，虽然比较次数相同。答题要写 fewer data movements / assignments。

ex.q: Key must move back 4 places. Count assignments in each version.
ex.a: Swap version: 4 swaps × 3 = 12. Shift version: 1 (save key) + 4 shifts + 1 (insert) = 6.
ex.az: swap 版 12 次；移位版 1+4+1 = 6 次。

cards.tz: 冒泡排序 Bubble sort：概念与步骤
cards.en:
Bubble sort starts at the first item and compares adjacent items; if a pair is in the wrong order they are swapped. After one pass the smallest item (descending sort) or largest item (ascending sort) has 'bubbled' to the end of the list and joins the sorted part, which grows from the back. Repeat for the remaining items.
Example [45,70,66,82,55,95,60], descending:
  • Pass 1 → [70,66,82,55,95,60,45] (45 at the end)
  • Pass 2 → [70,82,66,95,60,55,45]
  • Pass 3 → [82,70,95,66,60,55,45]
  • Pass 4 → [82,95,70,66,60,55,45]
  • Pass 5 → [95,82,70,66,60,55,45]
Bubble sort may do many swaps per pass, unlike selection sort.
cards.zh: Bubble sort（冒泡排序法）由第一项开始 比较相邻两项 (adjacent items)，次序错就 swap。一轮后，最小值（降序时）或最大值（升序时）会“浮”到 list 最后，成为 sorted part（由后面开始增长）。对余下的项重复。左边是 [45,70,66,82,55,95,60] 降序的每轮结果。与 selection sort 不同，bubble sort 每轮可能做很多次交换。

ex.q: A = [73, 85, 62, 96, 61]. Show A after the first pass of ascending bubble sort, listing each comparison.
ex.az: 4 次比较、2 次交换，最大值 96 浮到最后。

cards.zh: 降序 bubble sort 见上。外循环做 N - 1 轮。内循环比较 mark[j] 与 mark[j+1]，所以 j 最多到 len - 2（否则 mark[j+1] 越界）。内循环范围中的 - i 是跳过已浮到末端、排好了的项。< 为降序，> 为升序。pseudocode 常写成 for i from 0 to N-2, for j from 0 to N-2-i。

ex.q: What is the purpose of '- i' in range(0, len(mark)-1-i)? What happens if it is removed?
ex.a: After pass i, the last i items are already sorted, so comparing them is unnecessary. Removing '- i' gives the same result but makes more comparisons: (N-1)2 instead of N(N-1)/2.
ex.az: - i 跳过已排好的末端；去掉结果一样，但比较次数变 (N-1)²。

cards.t: Efficiency and improvements of bubble sort
cards.en:
Total comparisons with the '- i' version: (N - 1) + (N - 2) + ... + 1 = N(N - 1)/2. Improvements seen in exam questions:
  • Use for j from 0 to N-2-i instead of a fixed range: same result, fewer comparisons.
  • If only the top k items are needed, do only k passes, because each pass fixes one item at the end (for top 3: for i from 0 to 2, then read the last 3 positions, or scan right-to-left so they come to the front).
  • Scanning from right to left (for j from N-1 down to 1+i) bubbles the extreme value to the front instead.
  • (Enrichment) Use a flag swapped: if a whole pass makes no swap, the list is sorted and we can stop early; best case becomes N - 1 comparisons.
cards.zh:
使用 '- i' 版本时，总比较次数 = (N-1)+(N-2)+…+1 = N(N-1)/2。常见改良：
  • 内循环用 for j from 0 to N-2-i 代替固定范围：结果一样，比较较少；
  • 只需 前 k 名时，只做 k 轮，因为每轮确定一项；
  • 由右至左扫描（for j from N-1 down to 1+i），极值会浮到 最前；
  • （延伸）用 flag swapped：一整轮没有交换就代表已排好，可提前结束，best case 只需 N - 1 次比较。

ex.q: A bubble sort with a fixed inner loop 'for j from 0 to 3' sorts 5 items in 4 passes. How many comparisons? How many with 'for j from 0 to 3 - i'?
ex.az: 固定范围 16 次；改良后 10 次。

cards.en:
AlgorithmWhat one pass doesComparisonsNotes
SelectionLinear search for max/min in unsorted part, swap with its first itemAlways N(N-1)/2At most one swap per pass
InsertionTake key, shift larger/smaller items, insert keyBest ≈ N-1, worst N(N-1)/2Fast for nearly sorted data
BubbleCompare and swap adjacent items; extreme value moves to endN(N-1)/2 (with flag, best N-1)Many swaps
All three are simple and need no extra list, but their worst-case work grows with N2, so they become slow for large lists. Where the sorted part grows: selection and insertion at the front (left), bubble at the end (right).
cards.zh: 见比较表。三种都 简单，不需要额外 list，但 worst case 工作量随 N² 增长，项数多时会慢。Selection：每轮找最值再交换，比较次数永远 N(N-1)/2，交换最少。Insertion：取 key 移位插入，接近有序时最快。Bubble：相邻比较交换，交换次数多。sorted part 的位置：selection 与 insertion 在前面（左），bubble 在后面（右）。

ex.q: A sorted list of 1000 records gets 3 new records appended. Which basic sort is best to re-sort it? Why?
ex.a: Insertion sort. The list is almost sorted, so most keys need no shift; only the 3 new records move. It needs about N comparisons plus a few shifts, while selection sort still needs 1000×999/2 = 499 500 comparisons.
ex.az: 几乎有序 → insertion sort 最快，selection sort 仍要 499500 次比较。

cards.tz: 合并两个已排序 list：概念
cards.en: Merging combines two lists that are already sorted into one sorted list without sorting again. Keep a pointer to the first unmerged item of each list. Repeatedly compare the two first unmerged items, copy the one that should come first (the smaller for ascending) into the merged list, and advance that list's pointer. When one list is used up, copy the rest of the other list. Example (ascending): [45,55,66,70,82,95] and [43,69,85,91] → [43,45,55,66,69,70,82,85,91,95]. The merged list has len(A) + len(B) items, and the number of steps (copies) is exactly len(A) + len(B), with at most len(A) + len(B) - 1 real comparisons. This is much faster than joining the lists and sorting again.
cards.zh: Merging（合并）把两个 已排序的 list 合成一个已排序 list，不需重新排序。每个 list 用一个指针指向 第一个未合并项，反复 比较两个未合并项，把应排先的（升序取较小者）复制到 merged list，该 list 指针前移。一个 list 用完后，把另一个余下的项复制过去。例：[45,55,66,70,82,95] 与 [43,69,85,91] → [43,45,55,66,69,70,82,85,91,95]。merged list 共 len(A)+len(B) 项，复制次数刚好是 len(A)+len(B)，比先合在一起再排序快得多。

ex.q: Merge P = [98, 90, 71, 40] and Q = [95, 80, 52] (both descending) into descending R.
ex.az: 降序取较大者，Q 用完后复制 40。

cards.zh: 课本把两班升序名单合并的程序见上。i、j 指向两个 list 的第一个未合并项；k 是 merged list form4 下一个要写入的位置（form4 要预先有足够位置，如 form4 = [0]*(...)）。一个 if 就处理三种情况。条件用 <= 代替 <，相等时先取 class4A 的项；两者结果都是已排序的。

ex.q: Using the program, merge class4A = [2, 9] and class4B = [5, 6, 12]. Give i, j after each k.
ex.az: 依次取 2、5、6、9，A 用完后取 12。

cards.en:
At each step there are three cases:
  1. Normal: both lists have unmerged items; compare P[i] and Q[j] and copy the one that should come first.
  2. P is used up (i = len(P)): copy Q[j].
  3. Q is used up (j = len(Q)): copy P[i].
They combine into one condition, e.g. for a descending merge with 5 items in each list:
if i < 5 AND (j = 5 OR P[i] > Q[j]) then
    R[k] <- P[i];  i <- i + 1
else
    R[k] <- Q[j];  j <- j + 1
Order matters: i < 5 is tested first so P[5] is never read, and j = 5 is tested before Q[j] so Q[5] is never read (short-circuit evaluation). Missing these checks is a common error that reads beyond the end of a list.
cards.zh: 每一步有三种情况：正常（两个 list 都有未合并项，比较 P[i] 与 Q[j]）；P 用完（i = len(P)，复制 Q[j]）；Q 用完（j = len(Q)，复制 P[i]）。可合成一个条件（见上，降序、各 5 项）。次序很重要：先检查 i < 5，就不会读 P[5]；先检查 j = 5 再比较 Q[j]，就不会读 Q[5]（short-circuit evaluation）。漏了这些检查是常见错误，会读到 list 范围以外。

ex.q: In 'if i < 5 AND (j = 5 OR P[i] > Q[j])', explain what happens when i = 3 and j = 5.
ex.a: i < 5 is True; j = 5 is True, so the OR is True without evaluating Q[5]. P[3] is copied. This is correct because Q has been completely merged.
ex.az: Q 已用完，j=5 为真，直接复制 P[3]，不会读 Q[5]。

cards.en:
Sometimes the input lists and the required output are in different orders. If both lists are descending but the merged list must be ascending, start from the end of each list (the smallest items) and move the pointers backwards:
i <- 3      // last index of C1 (4 items)
j <- 4      // last index of C2 (5 items)
for k from 0 to 8
  if i >= 0 AND (j < 0 OR C1[i] < C2[j]) then
    ucard[k] <- C1[i];  i <- i - 1
  else
    ucard[k] <- C2[j];  j <- j - 1
Here 'used up' means the pointer has gone below 0, so the checks become i >= 0 and j < 0. The loop still runs len(C1) + len(C2) = 9 times. Practise rewriting the condition for each combination of input and output order.
cards.zh: 有时输入 list 与输出要求的次序 不同。若两个 list 都是 降序，但要合并成 升序，就由每个 list 的 末端（最小项）开始，指针 向前移动（见上）。这里“用完”是指针小于 0，所以检查变成 i >= 0 和 j < 0。循环仍执行 len(C1)+len(C2) = 9 次。要练习在不同输入/输出次序下改写条件。

ex.q: C1 = [9, 6, 2] and C2 = [8, 3] (descending). Merge into ascending using the backward method.
ex.a: i=2 (2), j=1 (3): take 2; 6 vs 3 take 3; 6 vs 8 take 6; 9 vs 8 take 8; j<0 take 9. Result [2,3,6,8,9].
ex.az: 由末端开始取较小者：2、3、6、8、9。

cards.en:
Merge sort uses divide and conquer and recursion:
  1. Divide: split the list into two halves, and keep splitting until each sub-list has one item (a one-item list is already sorted).
  2. Conquer / combine: merge pairs of sorted sub-lists (using the merging method of 6.4) into larger sorted lists, until the whole list is sorted.
Example: [70,55,95,82,66,45] → [70,55,95] [82,66,45] → [70] [55,95] [82] [66,45] → ... → merge [55,95] with [70] = [55,70,95], and [45,66] with [82] = [45,66,82], then merge to [45,55,66,70,82,95]. The syllabus only requires you to know that there are sorting methods quicker than the basic ones and to describe their idea; merge sort needs extra memory for the merged lists.
cards.zh:
Merge sort（合并排序法）使用 divide and conquer（分而治之）和 recursion（递归）：
  1. 分：把 list 分成两半，一直分到每个 sub-list 只有 一项（一项的 list 本身已排好）；
  2. 合：用 6.4 的合并方法把两个已排序 sub-list merge 成较大的已排序 list，直到整个 list 排好。
课程只要求知道有比基本排序 更快的方法并能描述其概念；merge sort 合并时需要额外记忆体。

ex.q: Show the split and merge steps of merge sort on [38, 27, 43, 3].

cards.en:
Quick sort also uses divide and conquer and recursion:
  1. Choose a pivot, e.g. the first item (any item can be used).
  2. Partition the rest into two sub-lists: items smaller than the pivot and items greater than or equal to the pivot. The pivot is then in its final position between them.
  3. Repeat on each sub-list until every sub-list has at most one item.
Example: [70,55,95,82,66,45], pivot 70 → [55,66,45] 70 [95,82]. Then [55,66,45] with pivot 55 → [45] 55 [66]; [95,82] with pivot 95 → [82] 95. Result [45,55,66,70,82,95]. Unlike merge sort, the work is done while splitting, and no merge step is needed.
cards.zh:
Quick sort（快速排序法）同样用 divide and conquer 和 recursion：
  1. 选一个 pivot（枢轴），例如第一项（其实任何一项都可以）；
  2. 把其余项 分成两个 sub-list：小于 pivot 及 大于或等于 pivot，pivot 就落在两者之间的最终位置；
  3. 对每个 sub-list 重复，直到每个最多一项。
与 merge sort 不同，quick sort 的工作在 分拆时完成，不需要合并步骤。

ex.q: Apply one partition step of quick sort to [40, 75, 12, 40, 63, 8] with the first item as pivot.
ex.a: Pivot 40. Smaller: [12, 8]; greater or equal: [75, 40, 63]. Result: [12, 8] 40 [75, 40, 63]; then sort each part recursively.

cards.t: Efficiency of merge sort and quick sort
cards.tz: Merge sort / Quick sort 效率 N log₂N
cards.en: Enrichment. Repeatedly halving a list of N items until each part has one item takes i levels where N/2i = 1, i.e. log2N levels. At each level about N comparisons are made in total (merging all sub-lists of that level, or partitioning them). So the total work is about N log2N comparisons, the figure the textbook uses for comparing with the basic sorts. (Strictly, quick sort can be slower, about N2/2, if the pivot is always the smallest or largest item, e.g. an already-sorted list with first-item pivot; you only need to know the N log2N figure.) For N = 1024: log21024 = 10, so about 10 240 comparisons, compared with 1024 × 1023 / 2 = 523 776 for selection sort.
cards.zh: 延伸内容。N 项不断对半分，到每份一项共需 log₂N 层（N/2i = 1）。每层合计约 N 次比较（合并或分拆该层所有 sub-list）。所以总共约 N log₂N 次，课本用这个数与基本排序比较。（严格来说，若 pivot 每次都是最小或最大值，例如已排序 list 用第一项作 pivot，quick sort 会慢到约 N²/2；考试只需知道 N log₂N。）N = 1024：log₂1024 = 10，约 10 240 次，而 selection sort 要 1024×1023/2 = 523 776 次。

ex.q: Estimate comparisons for N = 100 for merge sort and for bubble sort.
ex.az: merge sort ≈ 664，bubble sort = 4950。

cards.en:
Worst-case number of comparisons:
  • Selection, insertion and bubble sort: N(N - 1)/2, which grows like N2.
  • Merge sort and quick sort: about N log2N.
NN(N-1)/2N log2N
104533
1004 950664
1 000499 5009 966
For small N the difference is small (and the simple algorithms are easier to write), but the more items there are, the greater the advantage of merge sort and quick sort (textbook Fig 6.5). Exam phrase: 'For a large amount of data, merge sort / quick sort is more efficient because the number of comparisons grows as N log2N instead of N2.'
cards.zh: Worst case 比较次数：selection、insertion、bubble sort 为 N(N-1)/2，随 N² 增长；merge sort、quick sort 约 N log₂N。见表。N 小时差别不大（简单算法也较易编写），但 项数越多，merge sort 与 quick sort 的优势越大（课本 Fig 6.5）。答题句子：For a large amount of data, merge sort / quick sort is more efficient because the number of comparisons grows as N log₂N instead of N².

ex.q: A program sorts 50 000 records. Compare the worst-case comparisons of insertion sort and merge sort.
ex.az: insertion 约 12.5 亿次；merge 约 78 万次。

cards.tz: 为何有那么多排序算法
cards.en:
Misconception: 'We only need the fastest sorting algorithm and can forget the others.' Correct: no algorithm is best in every situation. Performance depends on:
  • the amount of data (for a few items, a simple sort is fast enough and easier to write and debug);
  • whether the data are already nearly sorted (insertion sort is then very fast, while basic quick sort can become slow);
  • the data structure used to store the data and the memory available (merge sort needs an extra list);
  • the cost of moving data (selection sort makes at most N - 1 swaps).
So programmers choose an algorithm that suits the situation.
cards.zh: 误解：只要用最快的排序算法，其他都不用学。正确：没有一种算法在所有情况下都最好。表现取决于：数据量（项数少时简单排序已够快，又容易编写和除错）；数据是否 已接近有序（insertion sort 很快，基本 quick sort 反而会慢）；储存数据的 data structure 及可用 记忆体（merge sort 需要额外 list）；搬动数据的成本（selection sort 最多 N-1 次交换）。所以程序员按情况选择算法。

ex.q: Suggest a suitable sorting algorithm for (a) sorting 8 scores on a scoreboard (b) re-sorting a sorted list after adding 2 items (c) sorting 1 million log records.
ex.a: (a) Any simple sort, e.g. bubble/selection: N is tiny, easy to code. (b) Insertion sort: nearly sorted. (c) Merge sort / quick sort: N log2N for large N.
ex.az: (a) 简单排序；(b) insertion sort；(c) merge/quick sort。
